name: Michelson–Morley
tested: Whether light's speed depends on the direction Earth is moving through space.
result: The expected fringe shift was 0.4; the observed shift was less than a twentieth of that. Light's speed did not depend on direction.

sources.label: Michelson & Morley 1887, American Journal of Science 34, 333

name: Ives–Stilwell
tested: Whether fast-moving atoms tick slower, by measuring the light they emit forward and backward.
result: The second-order Doppler shift matched the time dilation of special relativity.

sources.label: Ives & Stilwell 1938, Journal of the Optical Society of America 28, 215

name: Rossi–Hall
tested: Whether muons made by cosmic rays live longer when they move faster.
result: Fast muons survived the trip through the atmosphere far more often than their rest lifetime allows, as time dilation predicts.

name: Pound–Rebka
tested: Whether clocks run at different rates at the top and bottom of a 22.5 m tower.
result: The frequency shift was 1.05 ± 0.10 times the prediction of general relativity (later refined to 1%).

name: Hafele–Keating
tested: Whether atomic clocks flown around the world on airliners come back out of step with clocks on the ground.

name: CERN muon storage ring
tested: How long muons circling at 99.94% of light speed live, compared with muons at rest.
result: With a Lorentz factor of 29.33 they lived 64.4 µs instead of 2.2 µs, matching special relativity to about one part in a thousand.

name: Optical clocks at 33 cm
tested: Whether raising a clock by a third of a meter, or moving it at walking pace, changes its rate.
result: Both effects were measured at the size relativity predicts: about 4 parts in 10¹⁷ for 33 cm of height.

name: GPS
tested: Whether satellite clocks need correcting for their speed and their height.
result: They run about 38 µs a day fast relative to the ground (+45.7 from height, −7.1 from speed) and are built to tick slow to compensate.

sources.label: Ashby 2003, Relativity in the Global Positioning System, Living Reviews in Relativity 6, 1
